Salary & career reality

Aim high. Plan with both feet on the ground.

Salary is only one part of a sea career. Contract length, time between contracts, tips, rank and employer all change what you actually earn.

Indicative industry salary ranges by entry pathway
Starting pathwayIndicative industry rangesWhat changes it
Cruise hospitality₹30,000–₹90,000 / monthDepartment, tips, employer, experience
Merchant rating / trainee₹20,000–₹60,000 / month onboardVessel, contract, certification, vacancies
Officer progressionHigher with rank & sea serviceCoC, examinations, vessel type, experience

All figures are indicative industry ranges, not promises or verified NGA placement outcomes. Income tax, expenses and unpaid shore leave may apply. Ask employers for written offer terms.

Worth knowing

The parts ads often leave out

  • You may be away from home for months.
  • Shared cabins and shift work are common.
  • Medical fitness can affect eligibility.
  • Waiting for a contract does not mean a salary.
  • A “placement fee” is not proof of employment.

Straight answers

Before you choose a career at sea.

The questions students and parents should ask any training academy—including ours.

What is the total cost, beyond the course fee?

Ask for a written cost sheet covering tuition, registration, medical tests, documents, uniform, accommodation, food, examination and travel where applicable. [CONFIRM: Insert National Global Academy’s current fee and inclusions.] Do not rely on a verbal “all inclusive” statement.

Is a job guaranteed after the course?

No responsible academy can guarantee employment or a fixed salary. National Global Academy provides training and career guidance. Selection depends on eligibility, medical fitness, performance, documents, vacancies and the employer’s process.

Is life onboard safe, and is it suitable for girls?

Reputable shipping and cruise employers maintain onboarding rules, grievance channels and workplace conduct policies, but conditions vary by company and ship. Students—including women—should verify the employer, reporting channels, accommodation arrangements and contract before joining. Families should keep copies of every document and maintain regular contact.

What are the eyesight and medical rules?

Standards differ by role and pathway. Marine deck pathways can include colour-vision and eyesight requirements; hospitality roles have their own fitness expectations. Always complete the relevant assessment with an approved or employer-accepted medical professional, as per current DG Shipping guidelines where applicable, before paying substantial fees.

How do we avoid scams in this field?

Verify the institute and employer independently, read receipts and refund terms, never buy a “confirmed job”, and check official DG Shipping sources for maritime requirements. Be cautious if anyone pressures you to pay in cash, withholds documents or promises a visa and joining date for an extra fee.

What is the difference between Cruise Line and Merchant Navy careers?

Cruise roles centre on guest service, hospitality, food, housekeeping and shipboard operations. Merchant Navy pathways support cargo and commercial vessels through deck, engine and rating roles. Work environment, contracts, entry requirements and progression are different; choose by aptitude, not salary alone.
